title: Past-Due Balance Settlement Terms and First Installment, Repair and Emergency Service Calls
content:
## Terms

**(1) Who may ask.** A customer whose completed call under Repair and Emergency Service Calls still carries a balance more than 30 days after its completion date may ask to settle that past-due balance under a payment arrangement. The customer pays the first installment in person at once.

**(2) Single payment.** The number of installments is one: a past-due balance is paid in a single payment of the whole balance owing on the call when it is paid.

**(3) Later installments.** Under a payment arrangement only the first installment is due when the arrangement is made. Each later installment falls due 30 days after the one before it, and the balance stays on the call until they are paid.

**(4) First installment.** The first installment is figured on the balance owing on the call when it is paid. It is that balance divided by the number of installments, rounded once to the cent half up. An amount that falls exactly halfway between two cents is rounded up to the higher cent; for this purpose an amount within 1e-09 of a dollar below the half cent counts as exactly halfway.

**(5) Minimum balance.** An arrangement is open only when the balance owing is at least 750 dollars. A smaller balance is paid in one installment.

## Past-due test (hypothetical dates)

| Completed (day 0) | Request made | Days after completion | Past due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 1 July | 30 | No |
| 1 June | 2 July | 31 | Yes |

## Worked examples (hypothetical balances)

| Balance owing when the first installment is paid | Payment taken |
|---|---|
| $1,212.40 | $1,212.40, the whole balance in a single payment |
| $746.10 (below 750 dollars) | $746.10 in one installment |
